[Problem]{.card-kicker} **GCD Arrays** [CF 1629B · GCD Arrays](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1629/B){rating="800"}

To make $\gcd > 1$ it is enough (and optimal) to make every element **even**. A product is
even iff at least one factor is even, so one move can absorb a single odd number: multiply it
by any even and the even "survives" (stays even) to absorb the next odd. Thus each odd costs
exactly one move and evens are free - the answer is YES iff the number of odds in $[l, r]$ is
at most $k$. The one degenerate case is a single-element array: no move is possible and the
gcd is the element itself, so it is YES iff $l > 1$. This is @sec-gcd-a6's pigeonhole in its
purest form - a big input decided entirely by a parity count.

[Solved in full in @sec-gcd-p5-parity.]{.card-link}

:::
